title: Build an Institute Database with SQL
description: Design tables, insert data, and write queries for a training institute database using SQLite
objective: Students will design a relational database with proper constraints, insert realistic data, and write SELECT queries with JOINs, GROUP BY, and subqueries

steps.title: Create the Database and Tables
steps.instructions:
Open **DB Browser for SQLite** (download from sqlitebrowser.org) or use **sqliteonline.com**.

Create a new database called `institute.db`.

Run these CREATE TABLE statements:
```sql
CREATE TABLE courses (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    duration_months INTEGER NOT NULL,
    fee INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE students (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    phone TEXT,
    course_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    city TEXT,
    enrolled_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES courses(id)
);

CREATE TABLE marks (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    subject TEXT NOT NULL,
    marks INTEGER CHECK(marks >= 0 AND marks <= 100),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id)
);
```

Verify: Click "Browse Data" — you should see 3 empty tables.

steps.title: Write Basic Queries
steps.instructions:
Try each query and check the result:

```sql
-- 1. All students sorted by name
SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY name;

-- 2. Students from Bhopal
SELECT name, email, city FROM students WHERE city = 'Bhopal';

-- 3. Count students per city
SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students GROUP BY city ORDER BY total DESC;

-- 4. Average marks per subject
SELECT subject, ROUND(AVG(marks), 1) AS avg_marks FROM marks GROUP BY subject;

-- 5. Students with course name (JOIN)
SELECT s.name, c.name AS course, c.fee
FROM students s
JOIN courses c ON s.course_id = c.id;

-- 6. Top 3 students by total marks
SELECT s.name, SUM(m.marks) AS total
FROM students s
JOIN marks m ON s.id = m.student_id
GROUP BY s.id
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 3;

-- 7. Students who scored above average in Computer
SELECT s.name, m.marks
FROM students s
JOIN marks m ON s.id = m.student_id
WHERE m.subject = 'Computer'
AND m.marks > (SELECT AVG(marks) FROM marks WHERE subject = 'Computer');

-- 8. Course-wise revenue
SELECT c.name, COUNT(s.id) AS students, c.fee * COUNT(s.id) AS revenue
FROM courses c
LEFT JOIN students s ON c.id = s.course_id
GROUP BY c.id;
```

For each query, understand what it returns and why.

steps.title: Write Advanced Queries
steps.instructions:
Now try these challenging queries:

```sql
-- 9. Complete student report card
SELECT
    s.name,
    c.name AS course,
    SUM(m.marks) AS total,
    ROUND(AVG(m.marks), 1) AS percentage,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(m.marks) >= 90 THEN 'A+'
        WHEN AVG(m.marks) >= 75 THEN 'A'
        WHEN AVG(m.marks) >= 60 THEN 'B'
        WHEN AVG(m.marks) >= 33 THEN 'C'
        ELSE 'F'
    END AS grade
FROM students s
JOIN marks m ON s.id = m.student_id
JOIN courses c ON s.course_id = c.id
GROUP BY s.id
ORDER BY total DESC;

-- 10. Students who failed any subject (marks < 33)
SELECT DISTINCT s.name, m.subject, m.marks
FROM students s
JOIN marks m ON s.id = m.student_id
WHERE m.marks < 33;
```

Verify:
- Query 9 should show all students with grades
- The top student should be Ananya with A+
- Query 10 should show Vikram (failed in Maths if added)

**Submit:** Your `institute.db` file + a `.sql` file with all your queries.
